$comment: The last state of the validation machinery AND ITS WIRING that somebody other than its author attacked. audit-system.py check 5g recursively hashes every .py under validation/ and .claude/hooks/, plus .claude/settings.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, and the contracts the checks read. When that hash is not named inside an audit report under validation/reports/, the audit errors. Update this only when an agent from the roster has actually attacked the change and recorded the hash in its report — never to clear the error.
honest_strength: PROCESS PROMPT, not enforcement. That is the verdict of the independent audit of this very check (validation/reports/2026-09-01__system-keeper-attestation-audit.md), and it is recorded here rather than softened. It fires at ERROR and exits 1, which the version before it could not. But every satisfaction path can be taken without any attestation occurring: editing the `machinery` field silences it, and nothing in the repository detects that — only two things read this file, the check and the sentence in CLAUDE.md describing it. It raises the cost of skipping the step. It cannot make skipping impossible. Describing it as enforcement would be the exact defect it was built to catch, so it is described as what it is.
why_this_file_exists: Twice on 2026-09-01 a check was declared working by the person who wrote it and was not. C-021: 53 tokens carrying an inert alphaModifier, inspected three days earlier and cleared in writing as 'does not need re-doing' while every existing check passed. C-024: 39 warnings driven to zero in an hour, where one closure had made the citation check 96% blind — brand.md writes its citations as inline code, which the new stripping deleted — and another was closed by naming a document as its own verifier. Neither was found by the author. Both were found by dispatching an agent that had not done the work.
the_rule: If you changed the checks, someone who did not change them must attack the result before it is committed. The author is the one person who cannot perform this check, and good faith is not a substitute — every failure above was made in good faith by someone who believed the work was correct and had evidence they found convincing.
what_counts_as_an_attestation: An audit report under validation/reports/, named for an agent in the roster, produced by an agent that did NOT make the change, and CONTAINING THE CURRENT HASH. The hash requirement is not decoration: matching on filename and date was defeated three ways in a single audit — a zero-byte file passed, an 'audit-TODO-placeholder' passed, and reports written earlier the same day were reused to clear a change made after them, because attested_by was never dereferenced. The report must also verify by RUNNING and by planting the defect each check claims to catch; reading the code is what produced both false clearances in the first place.
what_was_rejected: Two versions were deleted rather than shipped. (1) A metrics-delta check that fired on a large drop in findings: it could never fire, because snapshots record end-of-session state, which is always clean. The independent audit found the cause is worse still — collect-metrics.py parses the NEWEST __system-audit.md, which is dated 2026-08-27, so recorded gate counts have been frozen for five days and read 0/0/0/0 throughout (see C-026). (2) A first hash that covered only validation/*.py and .claude/hooks/*.py, flat. It missed the wiring entirely: deleting the hooks block from settings.json killed enforcement layers 2 and 2b with every check still passing, and os.listdir being flat left validation/adapters/carbon-react.py — the script with the worst defect record in this repo — unhashed.
attested_state: Attested 2026-09-09 by token-keeper, which made none of the changes. THREE rounds were needed and the first two REFUSED. Round 1 refuted the claim in colour_resolve.py's own docstring that an unparseable notation is always reported: lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch(), device-cmyk() and hwb() gave zero findings — C-058's exact shape inside the module written to close C-058. Round 2 refuted the follow-up claim that a catch-all 'closes the CLASS': border:, box-shadow:, outline: and text-shadow: hid an unknown colour function because the scan read only the first token after the colon, an unknown function inside color-mix() was invisible because the container name occupied the property slot, and a custom property was invisible. Round 3 confirmed both closed by replaying the exact payloads, and CONFIRMED the narrowed claim now in ADR-023 — that this is a list of properties, not a class — by demonstrating four colour-bearing properties absent from it. The delta covers collect-metrics.py (system-keeper, C-057), the new validation/colour_resolve.py, and audit-system.py check 6 and gate-b.py check 1 rewritten onto it (C-058, ADR-023). Corpus re-derived independently each round: 42 files, 5,831 colour literals, 0 off-token. test-gates.py 17/17. Hook and audit confirmed to agree by running gate-b.py as a subprocess, including agreeing where both are blind.

known_open_at_attestation.$comment: Found by the attesting audit and deliberately NOT fixed in the same session. Fixing them changes the machinery, which invalidates this attestation and requires another round; doing that unattested at the end of a long session is the exact thing the rule forbids. Named here so they are inherited, not lost.
known_open_at_attestation.E-2 cheapest-bypass: NOT CLOSED — a fix was attempted 2026-09-02 and an independent attestation proved it did not work (F-1). The failing branch no longer prints the hash, a --machinery-hash flag was added, and a 500-byte floor was set; the claim recorded alongside it was that 'every remaining bypass now requires deliberately composing 500 bytes of prose that is not true'. That claim is false. The new flag SUPPLIES the token and the audit's own output supplies the bulk: `(audit-system.py --machinery-hash; audit-system.py) > validation/reports/<date>__<agent>-audit.md 2>&1` produces 3,613 bytes containing the hash and flips 5g to '[INFO] attested by'. A filler variant passed at 718 bytes. Before the fix it was one command line with no prose; after it, one command line with no prose. The residual gain is conspicuousness, not cost. Recorded rather than re-attempted: the attempt itself is now evidence that this cannot be made enforcement, which is what honest_strength has said from the start.
known_open_at_attestation.E-1 contract coverage: The hash covers 1 of 3 files in design-system/contracts/. component.schema.json — which all 216 component-index entries are validated against — is blind. FIX: hash design-system/contracts/*.json.
known_open_at_attestation.E-3 check 2b is defeatable: Registration is matched on the command STRING, so `gate-b.py.DISABLED`, `true # gate-b.py`, or changing matcher to `Read` all pass, and permissions {"deny": []} counts as non-empty. test-gates.py passes clean under a neutered matcher — the same proves-the-script-not-the-wiring gap one layer down. FIX: resolve the referenced path and require it to exist; require the matcher to cover Write and Edit; require a non-empty deny list. RETEST 2026-09-09: the neutered-matcher variant reconfirmed OPEN by direct exploit. The other two documented variants (dead script path, empty deny list) were NOT RE-TESTED this round and are named as such rather than carried forward as fresh.
known_open_at_attestation.E-4 unrecorded guarantees: Neither the wiring check nor the attestation mechanism appears in coverage.json, and V-004/V-005 still credit test-gates.py alone.
known_open_at_attestation.W-1 the hash watches code, not claims: STRUCTURAL, found 2026-09-02 and the most serious thing in this pass. The machinery hash covers validation/**.py plus four wiring files. It does NOT cover validation/coverage.json, validation/corrections.json or validation/published-surfaces.json — the attester mutated each and the hash did not move. Both ERRORs that caused the previous refusal lived in exactly those files, and three of the five changes under review were edits to them: had only those three been made, no attestation would have been owed. The prompt watches the code and not the claims the code is credited with, which is the same shape as every defect in this ledger — a record believed because the thing next to it was checked. FIX: add the three ledgers to WIRING. Not done here because it changes what CI accepts, which is Gate A, and because doing it inside the pass that discovered it would put the fix outside the attestation that found it.
known_open_at_attestation.W-2 the metrics series disagrees with it: F-8 is worse than 'unreproducible'. The Stop hook wrote error: 2 at two consecutive turn ends; the same hook invoked manually 45 seconds later wrote error: 1, as did 12 direct audit runs across three environments. The audit is deterministic and a write-truncation race did not reproduce in 60 racing runs. It does not undermine V-022 — the marker stays truthful and the record is internally consistent, so 5i cannot see it — but the only human-facing gate series disagrees with every reproducible measurement, and METRICS.md renders four frozen rows as measurements with no marker (W-3).
known_open_at_attestation.W-3 the hash cannot see artifact-embedde: FOUND BY THE 2026-09-08 ATTESTATION, deliberately NOT fixed in the same session — fixing it changes the machinery and invalidates the attestation just granted, which is the exact trap this file's $comment describes. Check 5g walks validation/ and .claude/hooks/ and never descends into artifacts/. So every checker that lives beside the artifact it checks is invisible to the hash: verify-charts.mjs and verify-widgets.mjs (rewritten substantially on 2026-09-07 — the same day they were found to have three blind spots and a bar chart shipping at 1.45:1), and verify-encoding.py, which is a .py file and still excluded because the walk never enters the directory. The gap is structural, not an extension mismatch. It is currently bounded by the fact that nothing in CI or Gate B invokes those scripts — they are run by hand from the artifact directory — so they gate nothing automatically. That bound is also the reason it matters: a checker nothing invokes and nothing hashes is exactly the kind of unattested machinery C-021 and C-024 were. Closing it means either bringing them under validation/ and into CI, or extending 5g into artifacts/ — either way a fresh attestation.
known_open_at_attestation.W-4 the value-capture regex has two exac: FOUND BY THE 2026-09-09 ROUND-3 ATTESTATION, deliberately NOT fixed in the same session. _UNKNOWN_FN in colour_resolve.py captures a declaration value as [^;}\n"']{0,400}, and that has two independent escapes, both confirmed by planting. (1) A HARD 400-CHARACTER CAP: a colour function whose opening paren lands at or past character 400 of the value is invisible; the attester found the exact boundary by binary search. (2) A SEMICOLON INSIDE url(data:...) terminates the capture before it reaches a real colour function later in the same declaration — an ordinary CSS pattern, not a contrived one. Both are LATENT: zero matches in the corpus today. Neither was named in ADR-023, which documented only the property-list bound; the ADR now names them. NOT FIXED HERE because fixing changes colour_resolve.py, which moves the hash and invalidates the attestation just granted — the trap this file's $comment describes, and this session already spent three rounds inside it. FIX: raise or remove the cap, and make the capture paren-aware rather than terminating on the first semicolon. Either way, a fresh attestation.
known_open_at_attestation.W-5 the property list is a list, not a c: CONFIRMED OPEN and deliberately so — this is a stated limit, not a defect. ADR-023 says a colour-bearing property absent from _COLOUR_PROPS is not scanned. Round 3 demonstrated four: filter, text-decoration, text-emphasis, border-image-source. None is used in the corpus. Recorded because the previous two versions of this claim were OVERSTATED and both were caught; an honestly-bounded limit is a different thing from an overstated claim, and the difference is why this file exists.
known_open_at_attestation.W-6 the context bundle is UNATTESTED and: OPEN BY EXPLICIT DECISION of Agentic Designer - RP, 2026-09-10. validation/build-context.py (new), AGENTS.md (now generated), context/ (new) and a ci.yml step were added. Current machinery hash is 206b17abe9db78b4 and THIS FILE'S `machinery` FIELD WAS LEFT UNCHANGED ON PURPOSE, so check 5g keeps erroring and CI keeps failing at the audit step. That red is the correct signal: a check is owed. Updating the hash to clear it would be the cheapest-bypass this file documents as its own defining defect, and it was refused. WHAT WAS DONE: three independent attestation rounds by system-keeper, which wrote none of it, REFUSED the tool and found eleven real defects between them — hand-transcribed prose that never opened CLAUDE.md; silent wrong output at exit 0 on every missing source; a parser that published a CLOSED question as open; a lost durable fact; a non-self-contained bundle; substring heading matching that extracted a decoy section; no code-fence awareness; a sibling parser that dropped rows containing a pipe; an unvalidated rescue snapshot; table scoping that published a decoy as a genuine correction; and a required gitignored source that would have made CI fail on every push forever and silently disable every step after it. ALL ELEVEN ARE FIXED and each fix was verified by replaying the exact planted probe. WHAT IS NOT DONE: the FOURTH round was stopped mid-dispatch on the user's interrupt, so the final three fixes — snapshot self-validation, full-header table scoping, and removal of an environment-dependent field that had reintroduced the CI-breaker in a new form — were verified BY THEIR OWN AUTHOR. That is the one thing this file says the author cannot do. The most likely remaining defect class, named so it is inherited rather than lost: ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT CONTENT IN A STALENESS-CHECKED FILE. It has broken twice already. FIX: run a fourth round against the committed code.
known_open_at_attestation.W-7 .codex/ is a hand-maintained twin of: FOUND UNPROMPTED by the round-3 attestation. .codex/ holds a 14-agent Codex-format mirror with the 11 standing rules baked in and a copy of the hooks. Today it agrees with .claude/ exactly. Nothing generates it, nothing checks it, and it sits OUTSIDE the machinery hash, so it is invisible to the attestation mechanism that would otherwise catch drift. build-agent-briefing.py regenerates the Claude side only, so the first rules change makes a Codex-run agent operate on stale rules with nothing reporting it. FIX: generate both surfaces from one source and bring .codex/ inside the hash.
